title: Six exact slab-avalanche footprints interpreted from SPOT 6 near Davos

source.provider: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF / EnviDat
source.citation: Hafner, E.; Leinss, S.; Techel, F.; Bühler, Y. (2021), Satellite avalanche mapping validation data, EnviDat, doi:10.16904/envidat.202
source.permitted_use: Database reuse subject to Open Database License 1.0 attribution and share-alike requirements.

acquisition.basis: The data description bounds the avalanche period after snowfall began on 13 January and before the SPOT 6 acquisition on 16 January 2019.

normalization_method: Six source features were selected by immutable OBJECTID and copied without reprojection, rounding, simplification, or topology repair.
normalization_software: GeoPandas 1.1.4, Pyogrio 0.13.0, and Shapely 2.1.2 used for attribute selection and lossless Shapefile-to-GeoJSON serialization.

spatial_coverage.description: Exact aggregate bounds of the six registered source footprints; this is not a surveyed-domain boundary.

detection_limitations: Only six positive SPOT 6 outlines classified SLAB with aval_shape=1 are registered. Exact means the mapped start-to-deposit outline was clearly and entirely visible; it does not quantify geolocation error, guarantee detection of all avalanches, or establish absence outside an outline.

positional_uncertainty.method: The supplied data description gives no per-outline quantified horizontal uncertainty for these six polygons.

limitations: Satellite-image interpretations are qualitative evidence under the avycore contract, not field-validation ground truth.
Each polygon is a whole-avalanche footprint; it must not be scored as a deposit polygon and provides no independent release polygon for an engine run.
No quantified horizontal uncertainty or complete surveyed domain is published for these selected positives, so strict IoU and within-uncertainty endpoint metrics are ineligible.
The event time is bounded to a multi-day avalanche period, not known per feature.
Humidity is UNKNOWN in every selected source record; dry-slab regime is therefore not established by this inventory.
The regional new-snow total is not an event-specific release depth, and no wind vector is registered.
No event-day DEM is supplied; any later terrain used for modelling would carry unquantified temporal surface error.
